claims.text: Ab initio molecular-dynamics two-phase coexistence simulations can yield the melting temperature of a refractory material.
Two-phase coexistence simulations can yield the entropy of fusion.
Two-phase coexistence simulations can yield the enthalpy of fusion.
Two-phase coexistence simulations can yield the volume change at melting.
The proposed method reduces computational expense relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
A simulation cell containing solid and liquid phases allows the solid-liquid interface to evolve toward equilibration.
The solid-liquid interface enables natural phase-coexistence and transition behavior.
Simulating the solid and liquid phases simultaneously allows the system to reach equilibrium at the melting point.
The melting temperature can be extracted from the equilibrium dynamics of the two-phase simulation.
Analysis of energy changes associated with the two-phase state can determine the entropy and enthalpy of fusion.
Analysis of volume changes associated with the two-phase state can determine the volume change upon melting.
Melting properties from two-phase coexistence simulations compare favorably with results from full thermodynamic integration.
Finite-size effects can affect the accuracy of the proposed method.
The quality of the initial solid-liquid interface can affect the accuracy of the proposed method.
The choice of simulation ensemble can affect the accuracy or applicability of the proposed method.
Finite simulation-cell sizes may introduce systematic errors into extracted melting properties.
